flags.message: outcome.json records actual_disposition `granted`, but the disposing docket entry (Nov 13 2026) reads 'Petition GRANTED limited to the following question: ...' and takes only the Solicitor General's reformulated Question 1. codex-baseline and claude-baseline labelled the prediction `granted-in-part` because they expected exactly that limited grant; gemini-baseline labelled the same forecast `granted`. Under the exact-label rule I scored `correct` 0 for codex-baseline and claude-baseline and 1 for gemini-baseline, so the accuracy bit here separates the candidates on label convention, not on the forecast. Brier is unaffected (actual_granted 1). A maintainer may want to settle whether a cert grant limited to one question is `granted` or `granted-in-part`.

codex-baseline's staged retrieval_log.json holds eight calls, all reads of two provisioned briefs, while its retrieval.md discloses further calls (a statpack read, `fedcourts paths`, a failed web search and fetch for the 2024 Macquarie opinion, two CourtListener MCP calls on it). The log looks partial. The leakage grade is `not_applicable` on the forward mode and the disclosed queries, none of which concern this petition's outcome.

record/documents/questions-presented.txt as staged for me holds the petition's questions, but codex-baseline and claude-baseline both report that the copy they were given held a passage from the petition's importance argument instead. Both recovered the questions from petition.txt; no grade turned on it.
